The left expression abbreviates the right one; not object-language identity. Same role as the global editorial \(a\mathrel{:\equiv}b\), different glyph. Source presentations outside the restoration scopes also print the definitional sign as a bare := without this macro; those printings, and the non-definitional roles of := (instantiation, update, substitution, program assignment, algorithm step) and of ::= (grammar production), are registered by region in symbols-intake-p01-notation-binding-and-comparison-of-formal-w02b-p01-013.csv and read by def:p01-w02b-p01-013-colon-equals. Inside the restoration scopes this macro also prints three instantiation or witness lines (sec:qe-categoricity-02, sec:arithmetic-coding-01, sec:first-incompleteness-04) whose left sides are not new names, and the scopes contain a literal := algorithm step (sec:automated-reasoning-01) and ::= productions; those are registered by region in the same intake. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-08129}\(P\Leftrightarrow Q\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\Leftrightarrow}} & \textbf{metalinguistic biconditional between assertions}\par\textit{Scope:} global. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[def:p01-w02-p01-022-setting]{\ref*{def:p01-w02-p01-022-setting}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-08129}.\par Both operands are assertions of the metalanguage (membership, derivability, satisfaction), not names of formulas; it is the if-and-only-if of the surrounding prose. Distinct from editorial formula equivalence, whose operands are formulas. See def:p01-w02b-p01-013-statement-iff. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00727}\(\varepsilon_X\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\varepsilon_X}} & \textbf{Stone-space reconstruction homeomorphism}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 2 stone-duality. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-stone-duality]{\ref*{sec:p10-stone-duality}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00727}.\par Maps x to the ultrafilter of all clopen subsets containing x. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00728}\(X(h)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{X(h)}} & \textbf{continuous dual of a Boolean homomorphism}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 2 stone-duality. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-stone-duality]{\ref*{sec:p10-stone-duality}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00728}.\par For h from B to C sends an ultrafilter of C to its inverse image under h, an ultrafilter of B. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00729}\(\operatorname{Clop}(g)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\operatorname{Clop}(g)}} & \textbf{Boolean dual of a continuous map}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 2 stone-duality. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-stone-duality]{\ref*{sec:p10-stone-duality}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00729}.\par For g from X to Y sends a clopen subset of Y to its inverse image in X. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00730}\(\mathsf{BA},\mathsf{Stone}\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathsf{BA},}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathsf{Stone}}} & \textbf{categories in Stone duality}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 2 stone-duality. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-stone-duality]{\ref*{sec:p10-stone-duality}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00730}.\par Boolean algebras with homomorphisms preserving both bounds; compact Hausdorff spaces with clopen bases and continuous maps; trivial and empty objects are allowed. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00733}\(\mathcal B_n,\mathcal B_{\rm cyl}\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathcal B_n,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathcal B_{\rm cyl}}} & \textbf{finite cylinder algebras and their union}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 2 stone-duality. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-stone-duality]{\ref*{sec:p10-stone-duality}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00733}.\par B-n contains all unions of length-n cylinders; the union is the clopen algebra of Cantor space and the direct limit of the inclusions. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00734}\(H:K\to X_B\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{H}} & \textbf{explicit Cantor-to-Stone homeomorphism}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 2 stone-duality. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-stone-duality]{\ref*{sec:p10-stone-duality}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00734}.\par Using a Boolean isomorphism alpha from B to the cylinder algebra sends x to the elements b for which x belongs to alpha(b). \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00739}\(R_f(U,V_1,\ldots,V_n)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{R_f}} & \textbf{canonical relation of a finitary Boolean operator}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 3 nonclassical-algebras. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-nonclassical-algebras]{\ref*{sec:p10-nonclassical-algebras}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00739}.\par Every tuple of elements from the successor ultrafilters has its operator value in U; for arity zero this is a unary predicate. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00743}\(\mathcal G^+,\mathcal A\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathcal G^+,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathcal A}} & \textbf{admissible algebra of a general frame}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 3 nonclassical-algebras. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-nonclassical-algebras]{\ref*{sec:p10-nonclassical-algebras}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00743}.\par The carrier is the Boolean family of admissible sets closed under complex operators. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00831}\(U\Rightarrow_X V\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\Rightarrow_X}} & \textbf{Boolean implication between subsets}\par\textit{Scope:} P10 legacy unit 9 doctrine-quantifiers. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p10-doctrine-quantifiers]{\ref*{sec:p10-doctrine-quantifiers}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00831}.\par The subset \((X\setminus U)\cup V\) is the Heyting residual in the powerset fibre. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-03004}\(E\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{E}} & \textbf{binary predicate constant for the empty directed graph}\par\textit{Scope:} P14 selected reachability comparison. \textit{Precedence/form:} n/a. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[def:p14-selected-reachability-model]{\ref*{def:p14-selected-reachability-model}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-03004}.\par Its empty extension belongs to the binary selected relation domain. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-03308}\(F(p,q)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{F}} & \textbf{formula coding the proposed proof-transformation graph}\par\textit{Scope:} P14 strength comparisons. \textit{Precedence/form:} n/a. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[thm:p14-strength-proof-transfer]{\ref*{thm:p14-strength-proof-transfer}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-03308}.\par Totality and contradiction preservation are premises proved in the named base; output uniqueness is not needed by the transfer lemma. \\

\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00923}\(\Omega,\omega,2^\Omega\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\Omega,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\omega,}\allowbreak\detokenize{2^\Omega}} & \textbf{finite outcome space outcome and event set}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00923}.\par The outcome space is finite and nonempty, and all its subsets are events. This first probability unit uses the full power set rather than a general sigma-algebra. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00924}\(p,\mathbb P,A^c\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{p,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathbb P,}\allowbreak\detokenize{A^c}} & \textbf{finite atom mass event measure and relative complement}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00924}.\par Masses \(p(\omega)\) sum to one; \(\mathbb P(A)\) is their sum over \(A\), and \(A^c=\Omega\setminus A\). A zero mass is permitted; almost-sure truth need not hold at every outcome. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00925}\(X:\Omega\to S,p_X,p_{X,Y}\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{X,}\allowbreak\detokenize{p_X,}\allowbreak\detokenize{p_{X,Y}}} & \textbf{finite random variable and marginal or joint laws}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00925}.\par A variable is a function on outcomes; its law is the induced mass function on its finite value set. Joint masses concern pairs of values, including unattainable pairs of mass zero. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00926}\(\{X\in D\},\{X=x\},f(X)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\{X\in D\},}\allowbreak\detokenize{\{X=x\},}\allowbreak\detokenize{f(X)}} & \textbf{inverse-image events and composition of random variables}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00926}.\par The braces denote subsets of the declared outcome space. The expression \(f(X)\) denotes \(f\circ X\); grouping over its fibers computes its law or expectation. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00927}\(\mathbb P(A\mid B),\mathbb P_B,p_B\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathbb P(\cdot\mid B),}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathbb P_B,}\allowbreak\detokenize{p_B}} & \textbf{positive-event conditional probability measure and masses}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00927}.\par Defined only when \(\mathbb P(B)>0\). The conditional measure retains the same event space, assigns zero mass outside \(B\), and renormalizes the masses inside it. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00928}\(H_i,E,\pi_i,J,\ell_i\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{H_i,}\allowbreak\detokenize{E,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\pi_i,}\allowbreak\detokenize{J,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\ell_i}} & \textbf{hypothesis partition evidence priors and likelihoods}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00928}.\par The hypotheses form a finite partition; \(J\) contains precisely the positive-prior indices. Likelihood \(\ell_i=\mathbb P(E\mid H_i)\) is defined for \(i\in J\); null blocks enter unconditioned sums with zero contribution. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00929}\(q_1/q_0,\pi/(1-\pi)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{q_1/}\allowbreak\detokenize{q_0,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\pi/}\allowbreak\detokenize{(1-\pi)}} & \textbf{finite likelihood ratio and prior odds}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00929}.\par The two-hypothesis odds identity assumes \(0<\pi<1\) and \(q_0>0\). Likelihood ratio and posterior probability have different meanings; no ordinary real ratio is assigned a zero denominator. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00930}\(p_2(h,u,v),\pi_h,r_h\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{p_2,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\pi_h,}\allowbreak\detokenize{r_h}} & \textbf{stipulated finite two-alert product model}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00930}.\par The three binary coordinates encode hypothesis and two alerts, with mass \(\pi_h r_h(u)r_h(v)\). The product specifies conditional independence under each hypothesis; one-alert rates alone do not establish that premise. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00931}\(\mathbb E[X],\mathbf1_A\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathbb E,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathbf1_A}} & \textbf{finite real expectation and event indicator}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00931}.\par Expectation is the finite mass-weighted sum. The indicator is one on its event and zero outside it. Linearity needs no independence; factorization of product expectation requires its stated hypothesis. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00932}\(\mathbb E[X\mid B]\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathbb E[\cdot\mid B]}} & \textbf{conditional mean given a positive event}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00932}.\par A real number computed using the conditional masses, with \(\mathbb P(B)>0\). It differs in type from conditional expectation given a random variable. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-00933}\(\mathbb E[X\mid Y],g(Y)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathbb E[\cdot\mid Y],}\allowbreak\detokenize{g(Y)}} & \textbf{finite conditional-expectation random variable}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 finite-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-finite-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-finite-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-00933}.\par A function of the finite-valued variable \(Y\), using conditional means on its positive-mass fibers. Values chosen on null fibers affect it only on a null event; they do not define null-event conditional probabilities. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01062}\(\Omega,\omega,2^\Omega,A^c\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\Omega,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\omega,}\allowbreak\detokenize{2^\Omega,}\allowbreak\detokenize{A^c}} & \textbf{outcome space outcomes full power set and relative complement}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01062}.\par The outcome set is nonempty. A complement is taken in that fixed outcome space; the full power set need not be the chosen measurable event collection. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01063}\(\mathcal F,\mathcal H,\mathcal C,\sigma(\mathcal C)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathcal F,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathcal H,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathcal C,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\sigma}} & \textbf{event sigma-algebras generators and generated sigma-algebra}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01063}.\par Generation is intersection of all sigma-algebras containing the specified collection. Finite union closure alone describes an algebra and does not imply countable union closure. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01064}\(\mu,\mathbb P,[0,\infty]\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mu,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathbb P,}\allowbreak\detokenize{[0,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\infty]}} & \textbf{measure probability measure and nonnegative extended codomain}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01064}.\par Measures may take infinity; probability measures have total mass one. The finite-measure condition is retained whenever subtraction or continuity from above requires it. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01065}\(\sum_{i\in I}a_i\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\sum}} & \textbf{nonnegative countable sum defined by finite-subset suprema}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01065}.\par Terms lie in the nonnegative extended reals and the index set is countable. Grouping includes empty sets and infinite values; no signed-series rearrangement is asserted. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01066}\(p,\mu_p\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{p,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mu_p}} & \textbf{countable atomic weights and their induced all-subset measure}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01066}.\par The event measure is the nonnegative sum of its point weights. Total weight one gives a probability measure, and singleton probabilities uniquely recover those weights. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01067}\(\mathbb N_+,A_m,Y,V,D_k\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathbb N_+,}\allowbreak\detokenize{A_m,}\allowbreak\detokenize{Y,}\allowbreak\detokenize{V,}\allowbreak\detokenize{D_k}} & \textbf{positive-integer model tails observations and large-jump sets}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01067}.\par The waiting example uses weights \(2^{-n}\), tail events, parity and reciprocal observations. In the separate CDF proof, \(D_k\) denotes points with mass at least \(1/k\), not a waiting-time event. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01068}\(\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d),\mathbb Q,d\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{\mathcal B,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathbb Q,}\allowbreak\detokenize{d}} & \textbf{Borel sigma-algebra rational endpoints and positive dimension}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01068}.\par Rational open rectangles form the countable generating collection in each fixed positive finite dimension. Real and rational closed rays generate the one-dimensional Borel sets. \\
\phantomsection\label{entry:symbol-registry-01069}\(X,(S,\mathcal S),X^{-1}(B)\)\par \texttt{\detokenize{X,}\allowbreak\detokenize{S,}\allowbreak\detokenize{\mathcal S,}\allowbreak\detokenize{X^{-1}}} & \textbf{measurable random element target space and inverse-image event}\par\textit{Scope:} P15 measurable-probability. \textit{Precedence/form:} meta. \textit{First use:} \hyperref[sec:p15-measurable-probability]{\ref*{sec:p15-measurable-probability}}. \textit{Registration:} p.~\pageref{entry:symbol-registry-01069}.\par The inverse-image notation does not require an invertible function.
